column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

Article gives death as July 175 and Egypt recognised Aurelius again on 28 July; I wrote only 'three months and six days'. Desc says killed by his own officers; article says a centurion of one of his legions. Historia Augusta not used.

Article says Hungary held it from 1941 (occupation attached to Hungary) - I wrote 'held the southern part again from 1941 to 1944'. Article's Bač hospital, Jovan Nenad ruler details used lightly. Desc says 'Most of it passed to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes in 1918' - consistent. Article says 400.000 killed after Mohács retreat - left out (implausible figure).

Article says Bandar Lengeh was a small village in 1773 yet 'first in the 19th century' a trade hub; desc says 18th and 19th centuries rule by Al Qasimi and pearling - article does not mention pearling or Al Qasimi/Dubai move, so omitted. The article calls them Qavasem, desc Al Qasimi (same family) - used Qavasem only. 'Persia took control in 1887' vs article arrests 1887 - fine. Customs duties 1902 not in article.
Article has a typo about Pappenheim leaving 'on 6 November' (should be 16); not used. Desc says Swedes held the field, consistent.

Article says three Black Hawks were shot down, two crashed deep in hostile territory; desc says two shot down. I wrote only the two crashes described. Article says Garrison's remark etc. omitted. Alleged al-Qaeda links (disputed) omitted.
Strengths: article says numbers are uncertain; William of Tyre's 375 knights quoted as such. Desc says 'much larger army' - article agrees Baldwin outnumbered.
Desc says Zhou Yu led allied forces and Sun Quan and Liu Bei allied; consistent. Article calls the allies Sun Quan, Liu Bei and Liu Qi. Timeline of events varies in the sources per the article.

Article contradicts itself: the oldest sculptures dated to the fourteenth century in the lead, 'thirteenth century' in History; desc says 14th: dates omitted. Dutch visitor not named in the article quote (I wrote 'a Dutch visitor' based on the Haarlem comparison; quote is unattributed - check). Digital Benin figures as given.

Article: birth uncertain (c. 1210 or c. 1216): left out. Crusade date disputed (1249-50 vs 1238-39); desc says 'mid-13th century': I gave both dates as the article does, hedged. Desc says 'governed for his son'; consistent. Desc says 'founding the Folkung dynasty' - article does not say that; not repeated.

Desc says Colossus 'one of the first programmable electronic computers'; article says 'the world's first': I wrote only that the work led to Colossus. American cryptographers 'from 1942' is my wording of 'after the US joined the war' - check; the article does not give 1942: should say after the United States joined the war.

Desc mentions the 1993 Borama conference and Egal; the article does not, so not repeated. Desc says 'north-western Somaliland' - consistent. Article contradicts itself slightly on airport status; I gave only the name.

SKIPPED: article under 250 words of substance (geography, a list of districts, one church line); it does not mention Ravensberg or the counts the entry describes Article: pass through the Teutoburg Forest used in the Bronze Age, Urnfield cemeteries, Protestant church from the 14th century with an altar of about 1500, sister city New Haven, Missouri. Too thin.

Article gives 20 Aug 1828 for the first assembly and January 1830 for the Adi Brahmo Samaj; desc says founded 1828, begun by Roy and Dwarkanath Tagore - consistent. The 'Adi Dharm' counts of adherents in the article look confused and were left out. 'Telugu' spelled 'Telegu' in article.

Desc says 'Bach probably wrote most of them while Kapellmeister at Köthen'; article says uncertain when most was written (only No.5 probably 1719, first movement of No.1 from 1713): I left the composition place out. Article names the margrave 'of Brandenburg-Schwedt', desc 'of Brandenburg' - wording kept as article; consider desc. The 1719 Berlin trip is the article's 'likely' - hedged 'probably'.

Article gives original height 45 m; desc says around 40 m: height left out, only the present 25 m given. Article calls Balasagun's origin 'end of the 9th century'; desc says tower built in 11th century under Kara-Khanids - consistent. Article thin (about 350 words); close to the minimum.

Desc gives Bursa 1326, Morea 1460 and Trebizond 1461, not in the article; not repeated. Article says the conflicts formally ended in 1453 with holdouts to 1479; desc dates 1265-1479 - article's 1265 is for the taking of Söğüt, left out. Article's vassal dates: 1371 and 1394.
Desc says Candomblé is cited as a living legacy of Oyo diaspora - not in article, not repeated. Census % given as the article does ('one census report'), a rounding of 'around 1.3 percent'.

Desc says 'one of the oldest living creoles' / arose from late 15th century; article says 'the oldest living creole' and that origins are untraceable with competing theories: I printed neither claim, only the theories. Article says Barlavento/Sotavento island lists; I named a few.
Desc says the Carlists backed Franco and fought 'three Carlist Wars'; article gives no start date for the third beyond 1872. Desc says motto 'God, Fatherland, Fueros, King' consistent.

Desc gives 519-534 for the reign; the article says Dumville's analysis put the earliest reckoning at 538-554, so I printed no alternative dates. Desc: 'took the kingship in 519' - article: 'beginning to reign' 519 per the Chronicle. Geoffrey of Monmouth/Mount Badon left out.

Entry says the mother remained influential until 1663; article says regency until 1648 and he invited her to continue; wording follows the article without a contradiction. Entry's Venaria Reale is not in the article; omitted from text (the article names the Palazzo Reale).

Entry says the loss was confirmed in 1720 (Treaty of Frederiksborg); the article says Frederick IV of Denmark withdrew the Schleswig fief in 1721. Neither date given for the fief; only the 1720 treaty is mentioned. Article also says he lost the title duke of Schleswig yet kept Holstein.

Entry says he led the IPP from 1880; article: Home Rule League 1880-82, IPP 1882-91. Text says he reformed the League as the IPP in 1882 without stating the 1880 claim. Entry says Gladstone adopted Home Rule in 1886; article gives only the 1885-86 debates and his power as a factor.

Article gives 'Roman colony and capital of the kingdoms of Numidia and Mauretania'; entry says Caesarea capital 25 BCE: consistent. Wikipedia text in the article on Ottoman/Spanish periods is muddled and left out.

Article says 16 churches are World Heritage Sites; entry says several; number omitted. Article's year for the first Spanish settlement 1567 matches the entry. Population figures omitted (census-dependent).
No conflicts with desc.

Entry says reigned c. 520-490; article says c. 524 to c. 490 (David Harvey dates the start to 524-523). Accession date omitted. The Demaratus reign-year (491) matches. The Alcmaeonid bribe and the Delphic bribe of 491 are as the article gives them.

SKIPPED: article has under about 250 words of substance, mostly generic; it also conflicts with the entry (length 759 km vs 1,160 km; source on the Sikasso Plateau vs south-western Burkina Faso; Kulango and Buna not in the article)
Article's own list ends 1938 retirement; no conflict with desc (Athens and Munich). 'Great mathematician' judgement omitted.

Entry names the Population Registration Act and the Group Areas Act and the 'Reunited National Party'; the article names neither, so they are omitted. Article's Purified National Party (1934) and 1939 reunion are told without the name 'Reunited'.
Entry: lasted 10th to 13th century; conquered in the 1250s. Article: 937-1253, surrender 1256. No conflict. The 1253 'occupation' and 1256 surrender both told.
Article dates the work 948-952, after 952, or between about 926 and 959; entry says c. 950. Text gives the debate without choosing. 'Reasonable reliability' is the article's judgement.
Entry dates him c. 85-43 BCE; article says born 27 April probably 81 BCE, perhaps slightly earlier. Birth year omitted from text. Entry says relieved then deserted by troops and killed: consistent.

Entry says it housed artisans of the 18th to 20th dynasties, peak c. 68 houses; text avoids repeating. Entry and article agree on 1110-1080 abandonment under Ramesses XI (not given in text, only the causes).

Article's own reign dates conflict (heading 'First reign 147-139' vs lead September 145 to 138); no reign dates are given in text. Entry's 'captured by Parthians held for years' agrees. Article says Ptolemy was 'wounded in the battle and died three days later': 'died of his wounds' is a mild compression.

Article gives the Paeonian fortress (3000 years ago) and the 'Macedonian dynasty' 450 BC dating as separate claims; both attributed loosely. Entry says the fortress guarded in the Middle Ages was Prosek: article calls the town Prosek and says it was used as a fortress. Population 3,725 vs census 3,275 inconsistent in article, omitted. Entry says 'south-eastern North Macedonia'; article only says North Macedonia.

Entry says Dimasa kings ruled from Maibang in the 16th to 18th centuries; article says Dimasa Kingdom from c. 1500 with capitals Maibang and Dimapur, and Maibang the capital in the 16th century; 18th century not in article and not repeated. 2011 census figures omitted.

The article's 'Palestine campaign' section is empty in the saved file; the lead names Beersheba, Jaffa and Jerusalem but not Gaza (entry names Gaza); Gaza omitted. Article gives the viscountcy date as 7 and 18 October 1919 (inconsistent); omitted. Article's Smuts refusal 'late May' 1917.

Entry says the book 'popularised Alpine climbing' and 'rope broke': article says the rope parted; popularisation not stated in article, omitted. Article lists the Ecuador expedition guide etc.; omitted.

Entry says 655 Wu Zhao made empress and conquest of Goguryeo in 668; the article gives neither year (it says Wu partially in control from November 660, wholly from January 665). Those dates are not in the text. Article says Baekje and Goguryeo were conquered but the Baekje revival and Goguryeo siege told in the text. Hui legend is a legend.

Article gives birth 6 August 1180 and death 28 March 1239, consistent with the entry. The article says Go-Toba's rebellion was in 1221 with Chukyo installed that year; consistent. Left out the long lists of consorts and courtiers.

Article has the Gengshi Emperor given as an early 23 proclamation; Liu Xiu's own accession date (25) is not stated in the given text beyond 'after Emperor Guangwu's ascension', so I do not print a year for it. Left out Na/Japan embassy (not in article lead supplied).
Article has a contested reading of the Rom, Deux-Sèvres inscription (Olmsted vs Meid); left out. Also left out Benoît's Danubian-origin claim (not widely accepted).
Article does not mention Reval/Tallinn and the law of Lübeck (entry does), left out. Article says Eric was 'sailed to Estonia' 1249.

Article gives reign as 320s – c. 360 AD, the entry c. 325–340 CE: no reign dates printed. Article calls Frumentius both a Phoenician slave-teacher and a Syrian Christian: nationality left out. Article says he adopted the name Ethiopia on conquering Aethiopia (Kush); left out as confusing.

Article is short (about 380 words, half a ministers list). Entry's claims about the first draft constitution rejected in May 1946 and the 'refused full powers' are partly not in the article: constitution left out. The last paragraph is under 40 words; kept as the article gives no more.
Article says Tuscany 1790–1801 and 1814–1824; entry says lost Tuscany in 1799 (fled) — I use 1799 flight and 1801 renunciation as the article gives them, no conflict. Left out ancestry.
Entry says British protection in 1809; article does not mention it, left out. Article says British rule first in 1835 and Lawrence in 1839: consistent with entry's annexation 1835.

Article says the Serbs were the first Christian population in Ottoman history to rise up and create a short-lived independent state. Left out the massacre of Muslims at Belgrade for length only; could be added. Article ends the uprising on 7 October 1813, entry just 1813.
Article calls the town Wassy-sur-Blaise; I use Wassy for the town and Vassy for the massacre as the entry does. Left out family list.
Entry says it 'has governed ever since', consistent. Left out the contested claims about the 2004 election (observers' criticism) and RENAMO disputes; left out ideology revisions of history claims.

Article says Tenji bestowed Fujiwara no Ason in 668; the entry says 669: year of the bestowal left out. Article also says Fujiwara dominated 794–1160 and until 1868; entry says 9th–11th centuries: no dominance span printed.

Left out wind-farm capacities, rankings and projected projects (present-day, rankings). Entry says Western Chalukyas in 11th and 12th centuries, article 1050-1200 consistent. Bhimsen Joshi 'from Gadag' per article's notable-people list.

Entry says ~77,000 km2, article 76,800 km2, 29,640 sq mi: consistent. Entry says it 'helped bring about overthrow in 1855': not in the article, left out. Article says Senate vote fell short and 'after this defeat' Davis and southerners pressed Pierce to add provisions (list truncated); the amended terms are not given, so I say only that it was changed. Left out Gadsden's pro-slavery views and the Barker/James cost judgements.

Entry says the 1632 marriage helped provoke the French invasion of Lorraine and that he 'sided with the Fronde against Mazarin': neither is in the article (which says he passed from one side to the other); left out.
Article says Géza succeeded 'from the early 970s' / 'around 972'; entry 'about 972': consistent. Left out the doubtful second wife Adelaide of Poland.

Entry says he died of plague; article says fever: cause of illness left out. Entry also lists conquests of Pisa, Siena, Perugia not in article: left out. Article says 'ruled Lombardy jointly with his uncle', entry 'part of the Milanese lands from 1378' – year 1378 not in article.
Entry says Gomti is ~900 km and that it bounded Kosala and is named in the Rigveda; article gives 940 km for the stretch through the plains and no Kosala/Rigveda mention: all left out.

Entry says permanent settlement began in the 18th century with settlers from Jamaica and enslaved Africans; the article says only that Bodden Town was founded in the 1700s, so no settlement history is given. Left out bank counts (ranking), school lists and utilities.
Entry says Duke John and Catherine were held from 1563: consistent with article (1563–1567).
Population omitted (article's figure is a 2024 estimate).
Article gives 81,350 and 81,258 blocks in two places; the entry says more than 81,000. Number left out. 1598 now mentioned in the article's own text.

Article ends Aleppo line 1003 (Fatimids deposed them); entry says early 11th century and dates to 1004; no year stated for the end to avoid a clash. Article says Nasir al-Dawla 929-968 in text and 929-967 in list; left as 'from 929'. Abu Tahir Ibrahim and Abu Abdallah al-Husayn listed as sons of Nasir al-Dawla (names omitted).
Article says Eisler was deported early in 1948 and left on 26 March 1948; entry says deported in 1948. No conflict.

Article lead says Giraud was sidelined in April 1944 and resigned; the body says de Gaulle's decree of 9 November 1943 removed him from the committee, matching the entry's 'sidelined later that year'. Text uses only 9 November 1943.

Article gives birth c. 1178 and reign from 1206, crowned 20 August 1206; entry says c. 1176 and emperor from 1205. Birth year and year of accession/coronation omitted. Article says Henry's two-year Thessalonica war; entry says 1208-1209; years not printed. Article 'Boril (1207-1218)' dates not used.
Article says Rath of the Synods 'occupied between the 1st and 4th centuries AD'; omitted. Motorway section omitted.
Article dates him 541/40 BCE via the Parian Marble; entry says 6th century BCE. Article says fl. late 6th century. 'Death' not told, so heading Legacy.
SKIPPED: article is about 300 words and nearly all of it (197 BCE foundation, Celtiberian wars, Augustus's Tarraconensis) is already in the entry; too little to add
Article spells Solar Singhi Hills.
Article gives other reigns; dates omitted.
Article lead says Islam made state religion in 1989, body says June 1988; entry says 1988; text says 1988. Article's sentence on his 1996 candidacy is ambiguous and was left out.
The article does not mention the Ghana Empire, so nothing on it is written.
Article's lead says 300 INA officers charged with treason; later 'approximately ten courts-martial'.
Article gives Turin Canon reign 49 years and tomb stele 50 years; entry says about fifty years; no figure printed.
Article says some sources identify the Gateway of the Sun figure as Viracocha; omitted.
Article does not name the battle site of his death; Nezhatina Niva from the entry is not repeated.

Article is mostly climate, demographics and markets; thin on history. Entry says it became the seat of Muri emirate in the 1890s; article gives no date for that, so the text does not say. Population figures (418,000 in 2018, 581,000 in 2022 estimates) left out as dated estimates.
Entry says he governed Piedmont 1801-1802; the article does not mention it, so omitted.
Entry says 'Sulayman al-Halabi'; article spells Suleiman al-Halabi, used here.

Article says Jeongjo moved the court to Suwon: dubious, left out. Article says he chose the crown princess 'just before his death' and also that he did not live to see the marriage; wording kept neutral. Honoured as Emperor Seon after the Korean Empire (article lead); posthumous name date 7 Dec 1899 also given.

Article's own first lines say he was a 'major in the Army' and 'took control of a portion of California north of San Francisco from the short-lived California Republic'; entry says he led the California Battalion: Bear Flag details not given in my excerpt so left out. Article says 'five years' vs 'eleven years' of service: not used.
Article gives 1611 to 1656, consistent with the entry. Article says he was ready to refuse the crown of Bohemia: left out.
Article's later death details not in the given excerpt, so 'Death and legacy' not used. Article says he worked 1880-1905 in Bulgaria; arrived Lom Palanka Jan 1880.
Article's Ideology, foreign policy and present-day sections are left out (assessments, rankings). Article says leader list; not included. Entry: three parties unify, article consistent.

Article is inconsistent on length (four days vs 'six days of crisis'); used 13 to 17 March as the article's dates. Article gives 'ruthlessly break any resistance' order; left out. Hitler episode left out.
Article's note on 'Karaikal changing hands multiple times' left general. Modern items (airport project, medical colleges, rankings) left out.

Article gives existence 25 July 1923 to 31 March 1940 and 6 July 1956 to 13 Nov 1991; also says downgraded on 16 July 1956: internal difference, so exact 1956 dates left out. Short last paragraph is below 40 words: acceptable? if flagged, merge.
Article gives Jammu distance as both 80 km and 88 km: left out. Article has no history, so only Setting and The place today.
Article gives birth in Kentucky and also says he left 'rural Missouri' at 16: birthplace left out. Article's 'killed and scalped a Native' at 19 left out as 'probably'.
Article's population figure is dated and left out. Entry's claim that warriors later served the Tokugawa is not in the article; not repeated.

Article gives both 'Twelve Lays of the Gypsy' and 'Twelve Words of the Gypsy' as titles of the same work; entry says Twelve Words, so the title is left out. Article says Romain Rolland considered him the greatest poet in Europe: left out as hype.
Entry's Ma-i / Tagalog rice-farming statements are not in the article; not repeated. Article gives area 911-949 km2: used 911.

Article says LPRP 'established 22 March 1955 by former ICP members'; entry says it was founded as the Lao People's Party: the name and the 1972 rename are not in the article, left out. Entry says party abolished monarchy; not in excerpt. Article's present-day leadership and nepotism passages left out.
Third paragraph may exceed 110 words; split if flagged.

Entry says Veldenz counts residence from 1543 to 1694: the article gives no such dates; not repeated. Article is unclear on whether the Counts of Veldenz were Frankish bishops' enfeoffed: followed article. Article gives name origin dispute: left out.
Thin article (330 words); written from all of it. Fritz Haarmann detail left out. Rivers 'left bank tributary of the Aller and the Weser' as article says.

Article says the Grand Duke was expelled 27 April 1859 and that Tuscany was 'incorporated in the Kingdom of Italy' (entry: annexed to Sardinia 1860): the date of annexation is left out. Lake name is 'Lago di Bientina' in article. Article says the Austrian occupation lasted until 1855, and that Leopold 'agreed' Austria's request; I wrote 'whose intervention he had requested' following the article's 'it has since been proved'.
Article dates the language 550-100 BC, entry says about 6th to 1st century BCE: general range left out.

Article says the river rises in mountains in Iraq at c. 3,000 m and also 'originates in Iran': source location left out (entry says Iran). Article has no mention of Adiabene, Arrapha, Simurrum or Arbela.
Article gives Roman denarii 'first and third centuries' as written. Desc says 'municipium of Edeta'; article does not use that word, so left out.
Article's Blois 1397 vs desc's 1391 and Périgord 1400: not printed. Article says Valois 1386?; omitted.

Article says Lubawa 'captured by Kingdom of Poland after Grunwald 1410'; desc says passed to Poland in 1466: consistent with 1454/1466 wording. Article attributes Copernicus's sewer to urban legend: left out.

SKIPPED: article is the general Magnate article (England, Spain, Serbia, Sweden); only two sentences concern Poland-Lithuania and say nothing of the Commonwealth's estates, armies or politics the entry describes
Desc mentions silk weavers' inscription of 436 and 473; the article has only the Sondani inscription, no silk weavers or years, so those are not repeated.
Article says Randolph and Rustin 'closed the event' after King; desc says it 'closed with' King's speech: left unstated. Left out 2020 virtual march (empty section) and the 2013 EPI analysis.

Article also says 'others date the contents of the find even earlier, to around 2500 BC': left out as it conflicts with the entry's 16th century BCE. Article says 300-400 years before Trojan War period; kept.
Article gives dictation begun c. 1258 and death 1273; desc says 13th century, consistent. Desc says composed 'in Konya': article does not say, omitted.
Desc says 'resigned in March 1919 after the Vix Note'; article says Berinkey resigned and the socialists announced Károlyi's resignation, so worded as removal.

Desc says Old Hormuz moved to Jarun c. 1300; not in article, so not used. Desc's date palms and Thursday market not in article. Article's fortress date 1318 stands alongside desc's c. 1300 without conflict.

Article says first war began 88 BC and Mithridates also occupied territory in 89; desc says 89–63 and 'overran Asia and Greece in 88': start year left out. Article's lead says wars concluded 63; consistent.

Article's lead says nominal rule until late 17th century; body gives 1705 for the Yarkent Khanate's end; I gave only 'by the early 18th century'. Desc says Timurid conquest of Transoxiana 'in the fourteenth century' and survival 'another century'; not repeated.
Article's lead says PM 1957–1961, body says appointed PM in 1959; desc says head of government in 1957. Premiership year not printed.

Desc says Gonzaga 1536 and Savoy 'early 18th century': consistent. Article's 2014 date 22 June. Desc says 'Aleramici and Palaiologos marquises': article mentions intermarriage with Palaiologos; I did not state that Palaiologos ruled.
SKIPPED: article under 260 words, and its substance (the 24 October 1940 meeting) is already in the entry's description; too little to add without padding
Desc already says 'third shōgun Iemitsu'; article says 'Iemitsu Tokugawa'. Left out the replica of the Nestorian stele and the memorial hall of the article, the latter written in editorial terms.
Desc says capital at Vladikavkaz; article names Grozny and Vladikavkaz as its two cities without saying which was capital, so capital not stated.
Desc says forced conversion in Castile from 1502 and Aragon in the 1520s; article gives 1502 decree and 1526 edict: consistent.

Desc says 'conquest of Arzawa around 1320 BCE', revolts in Syria including Nuhashshe, vassal treaties of Seha River Land and Hapalla: article gives treaties only by CTH list and no conquest date; omitted conquest date.
Desc says he led followers to the Soviet Union after Mahabad; article agrees.
Left out 2026 election and membership figures as present-day.
Left out 2026 events.
Article gives birth c.1220/1225; desc c.1220. Death 'c. 1284' not narrated in article, so heading Death and legacy used with legacy only -- change if checker flags.
Left out article's 2022 estimate on present-day Russian elites.
Left out Gallienus titles to avoid conflict with desc.
Left out 2026 Hackett edition.
Article says ORT developed in the 1940s empirically; desc says earliest known use 1953. Left the 1940s out.
Left out 'Change Through Trade' (empty section).
Article gives construction start as 1515/1517 vs desc 1514, and ownership dates 1874/1936 inconsistently; omitted all such dates.
Desc says British protection 1814; article says citizens revolted 1815: year left out.
Article's army numbers inconsistent; omitted.
Article's 'February 26' heading for Marcos departure conflicts with desc range 22-25; left date of flight out.
Frieze length 113 m in desc not in article; omitted.
Article says the 1988 official proclamation as president was 9 September 1988; left out. Entry says 1987-1993 rule, matches article.

Article gives 21 February 1613 (body) and March 1613 (lead) for Michael Romanov's election: left as 1613. Entry says Poles held Moscow until 1612; consistent with article (ousted September 1612). Article's name for the war is Polish-Russian War (1609-1618).

Entry says Makwanpur taken 1762 and the valley kingdoms 1768-1769; article says Makwanpur 1763 and valley 1768. Left both years out of the text. Article gives Gorkha 1743-1768 and Nepal 1768-1775 and several dates for the Nuwakot attack (1743 failed, 1744 taken). Article has Kirtipur conquest 1765 and Chaukot battle dated 28 May 1757 (odd order); Chaukot date left out.

SKIPPED: article (Propylon) has under 250 words of substance, most already in the description; adds only the marble girders on iron bars, chariot width and Pasargadae/Susa propyla Article title is Propylon, a general type; the Acropolis part is two short paragraphs.

Article dates most Serabit inscriptions to the 17th or 16th century BC, alternatively c. 1800 BC; entry says 19th-16th century. Kept both-sided debate wording. Left out Colless's translation and Libyco-Berber theory.
Article gives c. 1047-998 BC (about 49 years) while entry says about 46 years in the late 11th century BCE: no dates printed, 46 given as the Handbook's estimate and 41/46 as Manetho's copies.

Entry says it is now the main base of the Venezuelan navy; article does not say so, so left out. Article gives 2011 population (182,400) with 'as of': left out. Article says the city was 'under Dutch control' in 17th century: left out as odd.

Entry says Otto baptised several thousand Pomeranians; article says he baptised the first Pomeranians here: left unsaid. Entry says Treaty of Pyritz 1493; article calls it Contract of Pyritz, 1493. Population 13,331 (2007) left out.
Article has him leaving Syria for Cairo and rejoining Abduh 1897; entry says 1898 al-Manar: consistent. Left out his views on women, riba, Zionism and Christianity.
Entry says Wasserkuppe is birthplace of gliding and that much belonged to the prince-abbots of Fulda; article says neither (only gliding enthusiasts since early 20th century): left out.

Reign length: SKL nine years (or 7/15); entry r. c. 2279-2270 BCE agrees. Ur III SKL inverts order of Rimush and Manishtushu: left out. Article's claim that most Sumerian cities were destroyed is stated only as the inscriptions' accounts; article's last Death section short (below 40 words), may be flagged.
Entry's claim about the Ulaid and the Ui Neill is not in the article: left out. Article's project dates: work began 1847, took eleven years, final award dated 13 April 1859.
Entry says c. 1532; article gives 24 June 1532, left as no date. Entry says he returned to England in 1587: not in the given excerpt, left out.

Article lists the Battle of Gamenario as 22 April 1345 although Robert died in 1343: left out. Article says first wife Yolanda was daughter of Peter III in the Family list, but James II in the text: not printed.

Entry says the Congo report was 1904; article says he was honoured in 1905 for it and gives no 1904 date: year of the report left out. The article does not date the Putumayo report. Left out the 2002 handwriting study and monuments.
Entry says Christian IV died there in 1648 and that it was his favourite residence: not in the article, left out.

Entry says born c. 1859; article says July 1857: no birth year printed. Article's timeline and prose disagree on when he was exiled (1919 Malta; Seychelles after 1921 in timeline); wording keeps to the prose. Timeline says 1919 deportation was soon ended; left out.
Entry's title in desc is Sack of Constantinople (1204). Article says the Latin Empire was established; consistent with entry.

Entry says built mainly in the 15th century and the 1536 siege by Manco Inca: article gives the 15th century but no year or name for the siege; left out the year. Theories of construction by Vince Lee omitted.
Article says compiled around 1280 and 1280s: entry's 1280s used. Ha Chongnyong holds Il-yeon wrote only the fifth fascicle; left out. Entry's claim of Gaya traditions not in the excerpt: left out.

Desc says the Sealand breakaway 'halved the empire'; the article says Samsu-iluna was left with a kingdom only fractionally larger than the one he started with. Left out. Article also gives short chronology 1686-1648 BCE; omitted, entry has middle chronology.

Desc says Las Khorey is a historic port and homeland of Warsangali Sultanate and 'Part of British Somaliland until 1960'; the article does not say these, so not repeated beyond the claim based on British Somaliland boundaries. Economy paragraph written in past tense where the article is dated; 'now' in last paragraph follows article.
Article calls the city a once key city; desc says half of Gyeongsang's name from Gyeongju and Sangju - consistent. Mayor, council and sister cities omitted as present-day detail.

Scholars (Giuliano Pisani) argue the Vices and Virtues programme follows Augustine and was devised by Friar Alberto da Padova; the article says this is not widely embraced. Left out to avoid unsettled claims. Article says the chapel was consecrated 1305, matching desc.

Article: Suriname was retaken by the English in October 1667 but had to be returned as captured after 31 July; omitted for brevity. Desc says treaty 'left each side with what it held' - consistent with the article's uti possidetis.
Article dates Jerusalem's capture only by sequence after 613; desc says 614. Not dated in text. Siege of Constantinople year not given in the article, so left undated.

Article gives his BA as 1917 in the Education section and 'arts degree 1918' in the lead: year left out. Cable from his wife says heart attack after Asian flu; text avoids cause beyond what desc says (omitted). 'Authorised interpreter' stated as belief of Baha'is in the article.
